author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Build a per-game controller profile
summary: Preserve a known-good shared mapping, create one explicitly named game override, document its differences, assign it only to the intended title, and test isolation.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Jogcon controller configuration representing a game-specific profile for an unusual input device

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals
sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Write the exception before creating the profile

Export the working shared controller map, then open the target game by its exact serial and record the actions that fail under that baseline. Create one profile named with the title and region. Copy only the bindings needed to make the profile usable, change the smallest game-specific set, and keep a short before/after table so a later controller replacement can reproduce the intent.

Do not turn a title exception into the new global map. A complete clone silently freezes old dead zones, hotkeys, and device assignments, so later improvements to the shared profile never reach that game. The override should explain a real difference such as an unusual camera axis, a required pressure substitute, or a layout that conflicts with the common library mapping.

items: Shared profile passes a complete tester and ordinary game.
Target game's serial or exact library entry recorded.
Special controls listed with reasons rather than copied blindly.
Export the shared map and photograph its device assignment, dead zones, and hotkeys before creating the title override.
Use a scene that requires every proposed exception, then replay it with the shared profile to prove which bindings are genuinely title-specific.

blocks.text: Create and assign one scoped exception

items: 1. Export or photograph the complete shared controller mapping.
2. List only controls that the target title must handle differently.
3. Create a profile named with game, device, and purpose.
4. Apply the minimum changed bindings and leave unrelated functions consistent.
5. Assign the new profile to the exact game entry.
6. Cold-boot that title and verify all ordinary plus special controls.
7. Open a different game and confirm it still uses the shared profile.
8. Reconnect the controller and repeat both the scoped and shared checks.

blocks.text: Prove that the exception belongs to the game rather than the physical pad. Run the same controller and shared profile in a second title, then return to the failing action and enable the override. If only the named serial changes behavior, the scope is justified. If both games fail, repair device assignment or the shared map instead of accumulating per-game copies.
Accept isolation between shared and per-game input

Cold-launch the configured title and verify every changed action, both analog diagonals, Start/Select, and any chord used during play. Exit to the library, launch an unrelated title, and confirm it still loads the shared mapping. Reconnect the controller and repeat the target action once more; profile selection must survive device enumeration and app relaunch.

items: The override name explains its game and device.
Only the intended library entry loads the special bindings.
Changing the scoped profile cannot alter the exported shared baseline.
Keep a field-by-field diff showing that only the named serial's bindings changed and that the exported shared map remains byte-for-byte untouched.
After a cold app start, launch the configured game and one unrelated title; each must select the correct profile without manual reassignment.
Every game now uses the override: restore Shared as the default assignment.
The title ignores the profile: verify it is assigned to the exact regional entry.
Several profiles differ accidentally: rebuild from the documented shared baseline.
A controller mode change invalidates codes: create a separate mode-specific profile.

blocks.text: Detach the title from its override before deleting the experimental profile. Re-import the exported shared map, cold-start the same serial, and confirm that behavior returns to the recorded baseline. Keep the before/after table even when rejecting the experiment: it prevents the same ineffective binding set from being rebuilt under another name.

A per-game profile solves a documented title exception; it is not a substitute for maintaining one reliable common layout. Device IDs can change after firmware updates or Bluetooth re-pairing, so store the human-readable controller model and intended PS2 control beside the raw binding. Review old overrides whenever the shared profile or input backend changes.
